Moreover, the defendant did not rebut the, presumption of due service of said notice sent by registered post, contemplated in section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 by adducing any counter evidence. Defendant No.1 did not even examine himself as a witness to deny the evidence of Pws 1 and 4. 

 12. Since a reference has been made in the leave granting order in the unreported case of Haque Brother Ltd. vs. Mrs Gulfam Begum CP No. 314 of 1993 suffice it to mention that this Division by judgment and order dated August 26, 1993 dismissed the said petition for leave to appeal without laying down any principle of law therein regarding the service of notice under section 106 of the TP Act. An argument was, however made on behalf of the tenant-petitioner that the notice had not been properly served upon the defendant, inasmuch as the notice was returned undelivered with the remark "left" by the postal authority. But this Division did not find any material to disagree with the concurrent finding of the trial Court and the High Court Division that the notice sent by post at the address of the suit premises having been returned unserved with the remark of the postal authority 'left' was presumed to be good service. So far as the instant case is concerned, the High Court Division, in the facts and circumstances of the case mentioned earlier, did not even consider the presumption, although rebuttable, of good service of notice contemplated under section 27 of the General Clauses Act.
